title: The Best Museums in Tashkent
description: Which Tashkent museums are open in 2026, what each is worth your time for, and current hours and foreigner ticket prices, including the reopened History Museum and the new CCA.
body_html:
Tashkent has the best museums in Uzbekistan, and 2026 changed almost all of them. The national History Museum reopened after two years of reconstruction. The Temurids Museum closed for a rebuild in February 2026 and reopened in April. The museum to the victims of repression was fully reconstructed. A major contemporary art centre opened in a 1912 tram depot. The new Center of Islamic Civilization now holds the Uthman Quran. Meanwhile the State Museum of Arts, the city's main fine-art collection, is still closed. Most guides online predate these changes. This one is current as of November 2026.

At a glance

MuseumStatus (Nov 2026)Best for

Museum of Applied ArtsOpenSuzani, ceramics, jewellery and a beautiful old house
Centre for Contemporary Arts (CCA Tashkent)Open (since September 2026)Contemporary art in a restored industrial building
Museum of Victims of Political RepressionOpen (reconstructed 2026)The Soviet century, told through Uzbek lives

State Museum of History of Uzbekistan

If you see one museum in Tashkent, make it this one. Founded in 1876, the museum reopened on 24 July 2026 after almost two years of reconstruction. It now has new interactive and multimedia displays that run from the earliest civilisations through the Silk Road to the independence era. The collection holds more than 350,000 objects. Highlights include a Buddha statue from Surkhandarya dating to the early centuries AD, a reminder of how far Buddhism once reached into Central Asia. The building is an attraction in its own right: a Soviet modernist block from the 1970s at 3 Sharof Rashidov Avenue in the city centre.

  • Hours: Monday to Saturday, 10:00–17:00 (closed Sunday), according to the museum's official site.
  • Tickets: 100,000 som for foreign adults, 50,000 som for foreign students.
  • Photography: a separate permit is required, 200,000 som for photos and 300,000 som for video, so decide before you start snapping.

Center of Islamic Civilization

The vast domed centre beside the Hazrat Imam complex was inaugurated in March 2026. Its most important exhibit is the 7th-century Uthman Quran, which moved here from the Hazrat Imam square in November 2025. It is the most expensive museum in the city: a standard foreign adult ticket is 425,000 som, with an audio guide included. Visits run in timed two-hour sessions, and the centre is open daily from 9:00 to 22:00. Our full guide has the details.

State Museum of the Temurids

The blue-domed rotunda on Amir Temur Square tells the story of Timur (Tamerlane) and the dynasty he founded. It closed on 25 February 2026 for reconstruction and digitisation. It reopened in April 2026, timed to Amir Temur's 690th anniversary, with modernised halls and interactive and 3D displays. Hours and ticket prices since the reopening were not consistently published when we checked, so confirm them at the door. The building is worth a look from the outside regardless, and it pairs naturally with a walk around the square.

Museum of Applied Arts

This is often the museum visitors remember best. The collection of Uzbek decorative arts covers embroidered suzani, skullcaps, jewellery, carpets and ceramics from the 19th century onwards. It is displayed in a traditional house with carved and painted interiors, which are themselves the main exhibit. The museum is on Rakatboshi Street in the Yakkasaray district and is open from 9:00 to 18:00, with the ticket office closing at 17:00. Its weekly closing day was not consistently published when we checked, so confirm before a Sunday or Monday visit. It stayed open throughout 2026. In April it hosted a temporary exhibition of Timurid-era masterpieces. A small shop sells crafts, but compare prices with Chorsu Bazaar before buying.

Centre for Contemporary Arts (CCA Tashkent)

The newest cultural address in the city opened on 6 September 2026. It occupies a 1912 tram depot and power station, converted by the French architects Studio KO, and is described as Central Asia's first permanent institution for contemporary art. The opening exhibition, "Hikmah", brings together Central Asian and international artists and runs until 31 January 2027.

  • Hours: Tuesday to Thursday and Sunday 10:00–20:00; Friday and Saturday 10:00–22:00; closed Monday.
  • Entry: currently free. You register for a time slot online, or at the door if there is space.

The late opening on Friday and Saturday makes it an easy evening stop after dinner in the centre.

Museum of Victims of Political Repression

Set in the Shahidlar Xotirasi memorial park near the TV Tower, this museum traces Uzbekistan's experience from the Tsarist conquest through the Stalin-era purges, when much of the country's intellectual class was killed. It was fully reconstructed in 2026, with an expanded exhibition and new digital displays. It is a sobering, moving visit. The surrounding park and memorial are free to walk around. The museum is closed on Mondays and opens from 9:00 on other days.

Railway Museum

Opposite Tashkent's main (North) railway station, the open-air Railway Museum lines up steam, diesel and electric locomotives, carriages and equipment along a long stretch of track, and you can climb into many of the cabs. It is the city's best museum for children and a fun half-hour if you are catching a train from the station across the road. The official tourism site lists it as open Wednesday to Sunday, 9:00–18:00. See Day Trips & Beyond if you are travelling on.

State Museum of Arts: closed

Uzbekistan's main fine-art museum holds European and Russian paintings alongside Uzbek art. It has been closed for renovation since July 2023. In October 2026 the Agency for Cultural Heritage confirmed that it remains closed: a restoration project was approved in spring 2026, but funding and organisational questions were still open and no reopening date had been set. Don't plan a visit around it.

Planning a museum day

  • Mind the closing days. The History Museum closes on Sundays, and the CCA and the repression museum close on Mondays. Tuesday to Saturday is the safest window.
  • Group by area. The History Museum, the Temurids Museum and the CCA sit around the modern centre. The Center of Islamic Civilization belongs with the old city, alongside the Hazrat Imam square and Chorsu.
  • Budget for photo permits. Several Tashkent museums charge separately for photography, and the History Museum's permit costs twice the entry ticket.
  • Carry som in cash for tickets and permits. Card acceptance at ticket desks varies; see Money & Costs.

Two well-chosen museums, say the History Museum in the morning and the Applied Arts in the afternoon, make a full and rewarding day. It is the perfect plan for a hot afternoon in summer or a cold one in winter. For the rest of the city, start with Things to Do.
